title: Improving Quality of Genomic DNA from Tissue and Blood Samples Using Chelex 100 Resin
author: Singh, Kumari, et al.
materials: Chelex solution (200 μl of 5% stock) was added to 1.5 ml Eppendorf tubes. These tubes were heated at 100 °C for 10 min in a boiling water bath. Whatman paper discs with blood samples or the liver tissue samples were then added to the hot Chelex solution. The Chelex suspension along with the paper disc or tissue samples was further heated for 8 min, vortexed and again heated for 7 min. The Eppendorf tubes were centrifuged at 12000 g for one and a half minutes at room temperature. The supernatant was pipetted out gently to avoid extracting the Chelex resin as well. The yield and quality of DNA in each sample of the supernatant was measured using a spectrophotometer [Nanodrop 1000 (ND 1000 V3.8.1, Thermo Fisher)].

steps.title: Prepare blood filter paper discs
steps.instruction: Using a sterile 4 mm radius paper punch, adsorb ~5 µL of blood onto each Whatman filter paper disc (No. 1001917); dry the discs in a laminar‑flow hood for 30 min; optionally cut each disc into two, one, half, or one‑fourth pieces for testing, keeping pieces separated to avoid sticking.

substeps.instruction: Punch 4 mm radius disc from Whatman filter paper (No. 1001917) with sterile punch
Apply ~5 µL blood onto the disc
Dry disc in laminar‑flow hood for 30 min
If testing different amounts, cut disc into two, one, half, or one‑fourth pieces, keeping pieces separated

steps.title: Prepare liver tissue samples
steps.instruction: Excise liver tissue from the bird weighing 7 mg, 9 mg, or 11 mg, macerate slightly with forceps, and place each piece into a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.

substeps.instruction: Excise liver tissue weighing 7 mg, 9 mg, or 11 mg
Macerate tissue slightly with a pair of forceps
Transfer tissue piece to a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube

steps.title: Add Chelex solution and pre‑heat
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL of 5 % Chelex‑100 stock solution to each 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube and heat the tubes at 100 °C in a boiling water bath for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Add sample and incubate
steps.instruction: Introduce the dried blood‑paper disc (or tissue piece) into the hot Chelex solution; heat the suspension for 8 minutes, vortex briefly, then heat again for 7 minutes.

steps.title: Centrifuge and collect supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tubes at 12,000 g for 1.5 minutes at room temperature; gently pipette the supernatant into a clean tube, avoiding any Chelex resin.

steps.title: Quantify DNA concentration
steps.instruction: Measure DNA yield and purity of each supernatant using a Nanodrop 1000 spectrophotometer (software ND 1000 V3.8.1, Thermo Fisher).
